item.title: Multi-UAV Trajectory Optimization for Bearing-Only Localization in GPS Denied Environments
item.description: arXiv:2602.11116v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate localization of maritime targets by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) remains challenging in GPS-denied environments. UAVs equipped with gimballed electro-optical sensors are typically used to localize targets; however, reliance on these sensors increases mechanical complexity, cost, and susceptibility to single-point failures, limiting scalability and robustness in multi-UAV operations. This work presents a new trajectory optimization framework that enables cooperative target localization using UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras operating in coordination with a surface vessel. This estimation-aware optimization generates dynamically feasible trajectories that explicitly account for mission constraints, platform dynamics, and out-of-frame events. Estimation-aware trajectories outperform heuristic paths by reducing localization error by more than a factor of two, motivating their use in cooperative operations. Results further demonstrate that coordinated UAVs with fixed, non-gimballed cameras achieve localization accuracy that meets or exceeds that of single gimballed systems, while substantially lowering system complexity and cost, enabling scalability, and enhancing mission resilience.
item.dc:creator: Alfonso Sciacchitano, Liraz Mudrik, Sean Kragelund, Isaac Kaminer

item.title: Localized Dynamics-Aware Domain Adaptation for Off-Dynamics Offline Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2602.21072v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Off-dynamics offline reinforcement learning (RL) aims to learn a policy for a target domain using limited target data and abundant source data collected under different transition dynamics. Existing methods typically address dynamics mismatch either globally over the state space or via pointwise data filtering; these approaches can miss localized cross-domain similarities or incur high computational cost. We propose Localized Dynamics-Aware Domain Adaptation (LoDADA), which exploits localized dynamics mismatch to better reuse source data. LoDADA clusters transitions from source and target datasets and estimates cluster-level dynamics discrepancy via domain discrimination. Source transitions from clusters with small discrepancy are more likely to be retained compared with those from clusters with large discrepancy. This yields a fine-grained and scalable data selection strategy that avoids overly coarse global assumptions and expensive per-sample filtering. We provide theoretical insights and extensive experiments across environments with diverse global and local dynamics shifts. Results show that LoDADA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art off-dynamics offline RL methods by better leveraging localized distribution mismatch.
item.dc:creator: Zhangjie Xia, Yu Yang, Pan Xu

item.title: From Per-Frame Search to Practical Attacks: Investigating Adversarial Robustness of Multi-Agent Heterogeneous Cooperative Perception
item.description: arXiv:2609.17856v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Heterogeneous cooperative perception (CP) lets connected agents with different sensors and encoders share bird's-eye-view (BEV) features and align them through learned translation modules before fusion and detection. A malicious collaborator can perturb its broadcast to erase real objects from a neighbor's view, yet prior CP attacks assume homogeneous agents and rely on per-frame gradient descent that needs test-time labels, online detector queries, and slow backward passes. Porting these homogeneous attacks to heterogeneous CP exposes two further architectural barriers. Translation modules often block direct gradients, and heterogeneous fusion stacks use per-location fusion and detection heads that leave the standard removal-loss gradient zero on over $99\%$ of the attacker's message, so per-frame updates reach only the sparse anchor footprint while neighboring cells still detect the object. We present HetPoison, a practical feature attack that trains a convolutional generator once, offline, on a frozen surrogate stack to map channel-observable features to a bounded perturbation in one forward pass, requiring no labels, detector queries, or gradients online. Because the generator parameterizes perturbations across the spatial neighborhood rather than per coordinate, HetPoison overcomes sparse anchor gradients while amortizing search across frames into a $\sim$2 ms forward pass. On OPV2V-H, HetPoison lowers STAMP detection average precision from $0.899$ to $0.063$, outperforms 500-step Adam-PGD on HEAL, STAMP, and CodeFilling at up to $14{,}000\times$ lower online cost, and remains effective on real-world V2X-Real fleets and under cross-family transfer, communication delay, quantization, and unseen collaborator encoders.
item.dc:creator: Chenyi Wang, Yutong Liu, Qingzhao Zhang, Ming F. Li

item.title: StageVLN: Spatial and Trajectory Auxiliary Guidance for Efficient Vision-Language Navigation
item.description: arXiv:2610.05664v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) policies increasingly benefit from strong semantic priors provided by large vision-language models (VLMs). However, standard action supervision does not explicitly encourage intermediate representations to preserve scene geometry, relative orientation, or global episode progress. Incorporating depth estimators, explicit maps, point clouds, or geometry foundation models at inference can provide such structure but introduces additional computation, memory overhead, and architectural dependence during deployment. We introduce StageVLN, a training framework that shapes navigation representations through privileged spatial and trajectory guidance while preserving the original inference pathway. A frozen geometry foundation model provides multi-level spatial guidance to hierarchical navigator states, while relative-heading and expert-route progress objectives provide complementary trajectory-state supervision. All auxiliary components are used only during training and removed at deployment. On R2R-CE validation-unseen, StageVLN achieves 56.3\% SR and 51.4\% SPL with a 4B-parameter backbone, without an additional geometry encoder at inference. On RxR-CE, it achieves 54.3\% SR without additional navigation training data or a geometry encoder at inference.
item.dc:creator: Anh Dao, Quan-Dung Pham, Le Danh Vinh, The Anh Nguyen, Nguyen Viet Tri Pham, Yiyu Chen, Pham Tuyen Le, Van-Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen

item.title: A Geometric Perspective on Reward Function Updates in Inverse Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.14041v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) is classically solved using Lagrangian optimisation, by jointly optimising a primal-dual problem with gradient descent to obtain the optimal reward function parameters and corresponding optimal policy. While this algorithmic view of IRL has been highly influential, gradient-based reward updates only paint a partial picture, largely ignoring the geometry of the problem in occupancy space. In this paper, we present an occupancy-space view of reward updates in IRL. We leverage the insight that both the optimal solution and its geometry in occupancy space are known, and show that the geometry along the e-geodesic (straight line in occupancy space) toward the optimal occupancy directly affects the gradient of the IRL dual problem in reward parameter space. This perspective naturally suggests preconditioning the dual gradient with the average Fisher information along the occupancy trajectory. We show that this preconditioned gradient is just a convex interpolation of the old reward and a new target reward, yielding efficient natural-gradient-style updates with little additional computational overhead. We then analyse these occupancy-space reward updates from a Mirror Descent (MD) perspective, and show that policy search over the resulting rewards induces approximate entropic MD on the policy. Finally, we conclude with convergence results of such geometry-aware IRL algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Anish Diwan, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz

item.title: Kairos: Fast and Reliable Symbolic Task Planning for Autonomous Robots
item.description: arXiv:2610.39454v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Robots that plan while they act need a task planner that reads the models their designers write, answers within milliseconds, and says what each answer means. Models are written in the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), which has grown from classical planning to durative actions, numeric resources, time windows and continuous change, while planners cover one fragment each and differ in what their failures mean. The contribution in artificial intelligence is Kairos, a single planner, not a portfolio of existing planners, that covers the whole language and derives what each answer guarantees from the search that produced it. We prove when the exhaustion of a search shows that no plan exists, and give a relaxation of temporal tasks that proves unsolvability where temporal search cannot. For the compression of durative actions, we give a criterion on the values that actions read, prove that compression is sound, and show that it is not complete, so its failure is never reported as a proof. An independent validator checks every plan. The engineering application is on-line task planning for robots: Kairos is open source, packaged for the Robot Operating System, and the default planner of a widely used planning framework. On 1,756 public tasks from nine suites, Kairos solves more tasks than the strongest evaluated planner of each suite within 100 milliseconds, 1 second and 30 seconds; it proves ten of eleven unsolvable tasks, and handles each of the seventeen language features probed, where no other planner handles more than eight.

item.title: $\varepsilon$-WM: Error-Driven Dynamics Adaptation across Fast--Slow Timescales for World Modeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.15215v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to balance three key requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, rapidly correcting sudden changes; stability, avoiding lasting model updates from transient disturbances; and persistence, retaining adapted dynamics during the observation-free open-loop rollout. Inspired by multi-timescale predictive coding in the human brain, we propose $\varepsilon$-WM, a world model that adapts to unknown dynamics through error-driven corrections across fast and slow timescales. $\varepsilon$-WM incorporates three novel features: 1) Multiple internal experts (MiE) emulate neural pathway reweighting, each combining a fixed base expert with fast--slow adaptation networks. 2) Fast--slow timescale adaptation captures distinct adaptation dynamics: fast states respond rapidly and decay, whereas slow states accumulate corrections and persist. 3) Predictive correction uses prediction errors to update fast and slow states and reweight experts without gradients. During open-loop rollout, each expert feeds back its own predictions, and $\varepsilon$-WM aggregates their outputs through adaptive weighting. Extensive experiments show $\varepsilon$-WM has a consistently lower multi-step mean error than all ten baselines on six datasets, verifying the effectiveness of each feature.
item.dc:creator: Haoyi Zhang, Qi Zhang, Yunfan Ren, Yi Bin, Lei Zhu, Heng Tao Shen

item.title: AutoE2E: Don't speak - Language free end-to-end autonomy for L2++ ADAS and L4 Robotaxis
item.description: arXiv:2611.22374v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: AutoE2E is an open-source end-to-end driving model developed by the Autoware Foundation Robotaxi Working Group. It introduces a temporal bird's-eye-view (BEV) architecture that combines multi-camera perception, HD-map information and route conditioning to predict future vehicle motion. The evaluated model uses a pretrained camera-BEV backbone, temporal feature fusion and a lightweight recurrent trajectory planner. It contains approximately 79.9 million parameters, of which approximately 1.45 million are trainable in the evaluated configuration. The v1.0 release provides model checkpoints, training and evaluation code, and DataModelConsole, a dashboard for visualizing and inspecting model experiments. On the KITScenes validation benchmark, the fine-tuned checkpoint achieves an average displacement error (ADE) of 0.745 m and a final displacement error (FDE) of 2.020 m at a three-second prediction horizon. The paper also reports preliminary real-vehicle research conducted with the Technical University of Munich's EDGAR platform, alongside ongoing collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology. AutoE2E v1.0 is an early open research release. Its quantitative evaluation is open-loop, and the model has not yet demonstrated validated closed-loop autonomous driving. The release is intended to provide the autonomous-driving community with an inspectable baseline for further research, experimentation and collaborative development.

item.title: SparseHPS: A Unified Model for Human Pose and Shape Estimation across Depth Cameras and LiDARs
item.description: arXiv:2611.26730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recovering 3D human pose and shape from point clouds is central to motion capture, robotics and self-driving vehicles, because depth cameras and LiDARs sense a person directly in metric 3D and work under any lighting. However, current approaches are each tailored to one sensor type: point density differs by more than ten times between devices, public datasets are labeled with incompatible body models, and LiDAR approaches need long input sequences to offset sparse scans. In this work, we present SparseHPS, a novel sensor-agnostic network that recovers SMPL-X pose, shape and global translation from a human point cloud with one set of weights, for single frames and streams alike. Specifically, SparseHPS encodes the cloud with a LitePT backbone over sparse voxels, represents every joint by a learnable query decoded with one common head, localizes the body by voting over voxels, and draws temporal context from a causal memory of tokens from the seven preceding frames. A single model is trained on ten datasets that mix rendered clouds with real depth-camera and LiDAR captures, all converted to one body model. Experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art results on the SLOPER4D and FreeMotion LiDAR benchmarks, where SparseHPS lowers the root-relative joint error by 22% and 11%, respectively, compared with the strongest prior method, which needs 32 frames. On real Azure Kinect captures of held-out HuMMan subjects, SparseHPS attains a joint error of 34.7 mm. Moreover, the current frame alone already yields the bulk of this accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Zaychuk

item.title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
item.description: arXiv:2611.31822v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories. Building on Fast-WAM, which showed that video prediction shapes policy representations during training so that future frame synthesis can be skipped at deployment, we present G0.7, a generalist world action model scaled along two axes: extending the context window from a single observation to up to five minutes of history, and scaling pretraining to a large-scale corpus of robot teleoperation and human egocentric (ego) video. Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6x faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging. Project page: https://www.galaxea-ai.com/model-g07.html

item.title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM
item.description: arXiv:2611.32335v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Panoramic cameras capture nearly the entire spherical field of view in a single frame. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. We introduce GOLD-SLAM, a Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM system that combines high-quality rendering with accurate geometric reconstruction. It performs tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and uses tracked visual features in regions without LiDAR coverage to improve pose estimation. To address insufficient coverage of newly observed surfaces and floating artifacts during incremental mapping, we introduce Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP). To enable broader evaluation, we collect a new dataset, WHOLE, using a UAV platform across Weak-geometry, High-dynamic, Omnidirectional, Low-light, and Easy scenarios. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and WHOLE demonstrate competitive rendering quality and improved geometric accuracy relative to perspective systems. Compared with existing panoramic baselines, GOLD-SLAM improves mean PSNR by 5.56-9.10 dB and reduces mean Depth-L1 by 71.9-83.9%. To assess deployment feasibility on resource-constrained platforms such as UAVs, we evaluate an embedded configuration of GOLD-SLAM on a Jetson Orin NX (16 GB), demonstrating online operation at the cost of reconstruction quality.
